title: Big Tech's new AI dilemma: keep the compute or sell it?
excerpt: As the tech giants' AI splurge starts to hurt the balance sheet, selling compute is an easy fix — but they also need it to get ahead.
content_html:
As tech giants aggressively build out compute to meet the demands of the AI boom, some face a tricky dilemma: how much should they hoard and how much should they sell?

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg addressed the issue on the company's Q2 earnings call this week. While Meta doesn't currently have a business selling compute — the data center processing power used to run AI — to customers, Zuckerberg has said it's on the cards.

Zuckerberg said that a "significant portion" of its compute will go toward training Meta's AI models, powering agents, and growing its core business. "But we also expect to grow a large business serving large customers as well," he said.

Tech giants are racing to build out more compute to power soaring demand for artificial intelligence. Google and Meta both just slightly raised their capex forecast for the year, and Google signaled 2027 will likely be even bigger (in a rare move, Microsoft held the line on its capex projections).

All that spending is now showing up in the financials: Google's cash flow went negative in Q2 for the first time in the company's history, and Meta's plunged 91% from the previous year.

Selling compute is one way to offset that cash problem, but it also comes with an opportunity cost. The common refrain from execs across the companies is that there simply isn't enough compute to go around. These companies are racing to stay ahead in the AI race, and employees sometimes compete for access to compute.

It's a conundrum for Microsoft, too. As Business Insider's Dan DeFrancesco put it earlier this week: "Does it cash in on demand today or focus more on its long-term goals?"

On Wednesday's earnings call, Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said that "customer demand continues to exceed available capacity" for its cloud business.

'Foolish' to take a short-term profit

Zuckerberg returned to this problem later in the call on Wednesday. "Obviously, a common trade-off that we need to make is around how much do you monetize something today versus develop future assets for the future?" he said.

"It would be foolish to basically just sell all of the compute and take a short-term profit," he said, adding that improved intelligence would compound the value of the compute.

Hoarding too much compute could also be bad for the lucrative cloud businesses of hyperscalers like Google. "If you don't have enough compute for enterprises, they'll go right back to Amazon or Microsoft," said Bernstein analyst Mark Shmulik in a research note on Google last week.

Last week, Google said it would buy more third-party compute to satisfy customer demand as it builds out more internal compute for itself.

Google is also building its own chips, known as tensor processing units, or TPUs, which it is putting into other data centers with partners to unlock more capacity.

"Our first priority is making sure we are allocating what we need to compete at the frontier in terms of AGI development," said CEO Sundar Pichai on last week's earnings call, referring to how Google is using TPUs. "That is the foundation for everything we do."

While Google leans on its cloud business to boost growth, it also needs to hold enough compute for itself to protect its moat around Search, Shmulik said in last week's note.

Oh, and it also needs to keep developers happy and locked into its ecosystem, which means allocating — you guessed it — more compute.

content_html_zh:
随着科技巨头积极开发计算以满足人工智能热潮的需求，一些公司面临着一个棘手的困境：他们应该囤积多少，又应该出售多少？

Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格在本周公司第二季度财报电话会议上谈到了这个问题。 虽然 Meta 目前还没有向客户销售计算业务（用于运行人工智能的数据中心处理能力）的业务，但扎克伯格表示，这是有可能的。

扎克伯格表示，其计算的“很大一部分”将用于训练 Meta 的人工智能模型、为代理提供支持并发展其核心业务。 “但我们也希望发展一家为大客户提供服务的大型业务，”他说。

科技巨头正在竞相开发更多计算能力，以满足不断增长的人工智能需求。 谷歌和 Meta 都略微上调了今年的资本支出预测，谷歌暗示 2027 年的资本支出预测可能会更大（微软罕见地维持了资本支出预测不变）。

所有这些支出现在都体现在财务数据中：谷歌第二季度的现金流在公司历史上首次出现负数，而 Meta 的现金流较上一年暴跌 91%。

出售计算机是解决现金问题的一种方法，但它也带来了机会成本。 各公司高管的共同观点是，根本没有足够的计算资源可供使用。 这些公司竞相在人工智能竞赛中保持领先地位，员工有时会争夺计算资源。

这对微软来说也是一个难题。 正如《商业内幕》的丹·德弗朗西斯科本周早些时候所说：“它是按需兑现还是更关注其长期目标？”

在周三的财报电话会议上，微软首席财务官艾米·胡德表示，“客户需求继续超过其云业务的可用容量”。

获取短期利润是“愚蠢的”

扎克伯格在周三晚些时候的电话会议中又回到了这个问题。 “显然，我们需要做出的一个常见权衡是，今天的货币化程度与为未来开发未来资产的程度之间的关系？” 他说。

他说：“基本上只是出售所有计算并获取短期利润是愚蠢的。”他补充说，改进的智能将提高计算的价值。

囤积过多的计算能力也可能不利于谷歌等超大规模企业利润丰厚的云业务。 伯恩斯坦分析师马克·什穆里克（Mark Shmulik）上周在一份关于谷歌的研究报告中表示：“如果企业没有足够的计算能力，他们就会直接回到亚马逊或微软。”

上周，谷歌表示，在为自己构建更多内部计算的同时，它将购买更多第三方计算以满足客户需求。

谷歌还在构建自己的芯片，称为张量处理单元（TPU），并与合作伙伴一起将其放入其他数据中心以释放更多容量。

首席执行官桑达尔·皮查伊 (Sundar Pichai) 在上周的财报电话会议上谈到谷歌如何使用 TPU 时表示：“我们的首要任务是确保在 AGI 开发方面分配我们在前沿竞争所需的资源。” “这是我们所做一切的基础。”

什穆里克在上周的报告中表示，虽然谷歌依靠其云业务来促进增长，但它也需要为自己保留足够的计算能力，以保护其围绕搜索的护城河。

哦，它还需要让开发人员感到高兴并锁定在其生态系统中，这意味着分配 - 你猜对了 - 更多的计算。
